purpose: GOVERNING_PRINCIPLES.md rule 35's standing mechanical check (tooling/repository_hygiene.py's validate_no_embedded_absolute_local_paths) fails closed on every absolute drive-letter-rooted, Unix-home-directory, or WSL-mounted-drive path it finds in active, non-archived, git-tracked content, except a match in a structurally recognized non-live-pointer genre (test/fixture files, JSON Schema example values, markdown #Lnn review-evidence citations, regex pattern source -- all handled in code, not this registry) or a match explicitly registered here with a human-reviewed rationale for why it is illustrative/historical citation or a factual provenance record under rule 35's own carve-out, not a live structural pointer or self-reference. Each entry names the exact file, a stable substring of the offending line (line_contains), and the rationale a human judged it against. A sibling registry, ABSOLUTE_LOCAL_PATH_DEFERRED_SCOPE.json, exists for content this check's own construction found but explicitly declined to adjudicate (not the same as a citation -- it makes no compliance claim). This registry starts empty: the sweep that built this check found zero absolute-local-path embeddings anywhere in this repository's active, tracked content (drive-letter, home-directory, or WSL-mount forms), so no reviewed exemption was yet needed. A future absolute-path embedding that does not fit a structural exemption fails the check until a human reviews it and either fixes it or adds an entry here with its own rationale.
